Body: You've put the miles in. Now's the time to make sure your gear is ready for the next one.

End-of-season maintenance isn't glamorous, but it's the difference between pulling out fresh kit in spring and discovering a problem at the trailhead.

Start with your shelter. The Northbay Ridgeline 2P Tent (NB-TNT-02) is a 3-season, 2-person tent built from ripstop nylon and packs down at 2.1 kg — light enough to carry, substantial enough to matter. Before you bag it for storage:

• Pitch it once and look for stressed seams, small tears in the ripstop nylon, or pole sections that don't seat cleanly.
• Wipe down the floor and fly. Dirt left sitting breaks down fabric over time.
• Check the zippers. Run them the full length and work in a little zipper lubricant if they're catching.
• Re-stake the guylines and inspect for fraying.
• Store it loosely — stuff sacks are for the trail, not the closet. Compression over months weakens the fabric.

A note on limits: the Ridgeline is a 3-season shelter. It handles shoulder-season cold and moderate rain well. It is not built for sustained winter conditions or heavy snow loads — plan accordingly.

Take 20 minutes this week. Your spring-self will thank you.
